column3: “let them fall” renders “left (spread) them,” and NASB adds “deep”; the Hebrew “about two cubits above the face of the ground” may refer to the height at which the birds flew.
“spent” renders “arose”; NASB puts “he who gathered least …” in parentheses, and “they spread them out” renders an emphatic doubled verb.
“Kibroth-hattaavah” means “graves of craving,” and “who had been greedy” renders “who craved.”
